paper_title: Paper Copilot A Self-Evolving and Efficient LLM System for Personalized   Academic Assistance
caption: Feature pre-computation significantly improves the efficiency. The time cost for retrieval without feature pre-computation will grow with the exponential increase of paper number, while our proposed feature pre-computation stays unchanged and keeps constant time cost.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates time cost versus the number of papers for two retrieval settings, labeled “w/o Pre-computation” and “w Pre-computation,” to show how runtime changes as the paper count increases. The x-axis is labeled “Paper Number” and shows discrete values that double each step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256), spanning from 1 to 256 with one tick per listed value (visually equally spaced as powers of two). The y-axis is labeled “Time Cost (s)” on a linear scale, ranging from 0 up to about 35, with labeled ticks at regular 5-second intervals (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35). The “w/o Pre-computation” series is a solid blue line without markers that increases across the x-axis: it begins near 0 seconds at paper number 1, rises gradually through the smaller paper counts, reaches roughly 5 seconds around 32 papers, increases to about 9 seconds at 64 papers, then climbs more steeply to about 22 seconds at 128 papers and ends around 35–36 seconds at 256 papers. The “w Pre-computation” series is a solid orange line without markers that stays nearly flat close to 0 seconds across all x values (from 1 through 256), showing minimal visible change over the full range.
